problems.title: Minimum-scope (7,5) Difference Triangle Set
problems.objective: Construct seven normalized rows of six nonnegative integers whose 105 positive within-row differences are all globally distinct, minimizing the maximum entry (scope).
problems.true_objective: Find a valid (7,5)-DTS with scope no greater than 111.

baseline.meaning: Published valid construction; not asserted here to be globally optimal unless independently proved.

evaluator.contract: Check seven rows, six entries per row, first entry zero, strict row order, global uniqueness of all 105 positive within-row differences, and maximum entry.

problems.title: 12-point Heilbronn configuration in the unit square
problems.objective: Place 12 points in [0,1]^2 to maximize the minimum area of the 220 triangles determined by triples of points.
problems.true_objective: Produce a rigorously defensible 12-point configuration with minimum triangle area strictly greater than the frozen Comellas-Yebra baseline.

baseline.meaning: Published lower bound from an explicit 12-point construction. The source states that optimality was not proved; current record listings continue to treat it as best known.

evaluator.contract: Check 12 points in the closed unit square and all 220 triangle determinants; compare the minimum area to the exact baseline using exact or certified arithmetic.

problems.title: k=4 circle k-server potential discovery
problems.objective: Discover a potential function for the public k=4 circle/circle-taxi work-function formulation satisfying the required competitiveness inequalities.
problems.true_objective: Find a mathematically valid potential for the k=4 circle formulation, with finite benchmark progress treated as evidence toward the conjecture rather than as a proof of the full conjecture.

baseline.meaning: Reported best candidate under the pinned public formulation. A 17-violation human-designed baseline is also recorded in the upstream README.

evaluator.contract: The evaluator instantiates the candidate Potential and counts violations_k over the pinned precomputed instance; candidate code may propose potential_kwargs but may not redefine scoring or metric data.
limitations: The finite evaluator is sound for refuting a candidate on checked inequalities but incomplete as a proof of the full conjecture.
A zero count on one finite instance is not a proof and must not be reported as solving the conjecture.
The 3-violation result is reported upstream; this foundation does not run the multi-million-edge evaluator.
